question: A team is adding a new Claude-assisted output into an existing process and has to work out how much checking it will get. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Set the level of review that degree of risk requires; judge how visible the output is and how easily a mistake in it could be undone; have the named reviewer carry out that review; release the output to its audience.

B) Release the output to its audience; judge how visible the output is and how easily a mistake in it could be undone; set the level of review that degree of risk requires; have the named reviewer carry out that review.

C) Judge how visible the output is and how easily a mistake in it could be undone; set the level of review that degree of risk requires; have the named reviewer carry out that review; release the output to its audience.

D) Judge how visible the output is and how easily a mistake in it could be undone; have the named reviewer carry out that review; release the output to its audience; set the level of review that degree of risk requires.
correct_answers: C) Judge how visible the output is and how easily a mistake in it could be undone; set the level of review that degree of risk requires; have the named reviewer carry out that review; release the output to its audience.
explanations: The review level is being fixed before anyone has worked out the risk, so the assessment that should have driven the decision arrives too late to inform it.
Releasing first defeats the whole exercise. Any risk assessment and review that follow publication cannot prevent the harm they were meant to catch.

Correct. Visibility and reversibility determine how much scrutiny an output deserves, so they are assessed first; that assessment sets the required level of review, the named reviewer then performs it, and only then does the output reach its audience.
The review happens with no agreed standard behind it, and the level of review is only settled after the output has already gone out, which is the wrong way round.
